name: Juan II de Castilla
bio: Juan II (1405-1454) was King of Castile and León from 1406, the year of his father's death, until his own. His long and troubled reign was dominated by his favourite Álvaro de Luna and by the quarrels of the great nobles, but his court was among the most brilliant literary centres of its time, and he was a patron of the poets of the Spanish cancioneros, among them the Marqués de Santillana and Juan de Mena. He was the father of Isabel the Catholic.

He was himself a lover of verse, and a few short poems in the courtly style of the cancioneros are attributed to him. The best known is a canción on the power of love, 'Amor, yo nunca penssé', printed in the Oxford Book of Spanish Verse; John Bowring englished it in 1824 from the Cancionero printed with Juan de Mena's works at Antwerp in 1552.

poems.title: Amor, yo nunca penssé
poems.author: Juan II de Castilla
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Spanish Verse (1913)
poems.note: Spanish original; the English translation by John Bowring follows as the next poem.
poems.text:
Amor, yo nunca penssé,
aunque poderoso eras,
que podrias tener maneras
para trastornar la fe,
fastagora que lo sé.

Pensaba que conocido
te devia yo tener,
mas non podiera creher
que eras tan mal sabido,
nin tan poco yo penssé,
aunque poderoso eras,
que podrias tener maneras
para trastornar la fe,
fastagora que lo sé.

poems.title: I Never Knew It, Love! Till Now
poems.author: Juan II de Castilla
poems.collection: Ancient Poetry and Romances of Spain (1824)
poems.note: Translation of the canción 'Amor, yo nunca penssé' (the Spanish original is the preceding poem).
poems.text:
I ne'er imagined, love! that thou
Wert such a mighty one; at will
Thou canst both faith and conscience bow,
And thy despotic law fulfil:
I never knew it, love! till now.

I thought I knew thee well,—I thought
That I thy mazes had explor'd;
But I within thy nets am caught,
And now I own thee, sovereign lord!
I ne'er imagined, love! that thou
Wert such a mighty one; at will
Thou bidst both faith and conscience bow,
And thy despotic law fulfil:
I never knew it, love! till now.
